editorial.headline: Designing the World Before the Screen Comes Alive
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the specialist creative planning that gives film, video, television, animation and comics their narrative, visual and production shape.
editorial.body:
This activity is about the design work that happens before a screen project takes its final form. It covers specialist creative planning for films, videos, television programmes, animation and comics: shaping stories, designing characters and casting choices, setting artistic and visual direction, planning production’s technical design, and identifying supporting requirements. The work is formative rather than merely decorative; it provides the creative and practical framework through which a production can be imagined, organised and realised.

That scope makes it a natural home for studios, creative teams and specialist practitioners whose contribution lies in conceiving a project’s narrative, visual and technical language. It is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. The breadth matters. A small creative practice and a larger production-design operation may both undertake this planning work, provided the activity remains within the stated scope. The classification does not extend to the creation of comics itself, or to the planning and production of computer animation.

Nationally, the position is clear: the activity is TERBUKA to PMA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In other words, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level. That national openness should not, however, be mistaken for an automatic route to a Bali PMA registration. Bali’s position is materially different, and it is the distinction founders need to read first rather than last.

In Bali, this activity is Blocked (risk class) for PMA registration. At the Besar scale, every scope is recorded in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, bringing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The recorded block is tied to that moratorium as of 13 May 2026. The practical conclusion is direct: although foreign ownership can reach 100% nationally, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness to 100% foreign ownership does not create a Bali PMA registration route for this activity today.
